items.title: Chapter 1: Introduction to Insurance
items.description:
• Origin: Insurance originated in Rhodes (Greek island) — merchants pooled sea-voyage risks. Modern marine insurance began at Lloyd's Coffee House, London (1688).
• Definition: A contract where the insurer compensates the insured against losses, damage, illness, or death in exchange for a premium. Premium = the price of insurance.
• Risk Transfer Mechanism: Loss of a FEW is shared by MANY. All policyholders pay premium into a common pool; claims are paid from this pool — principle of pooling/sharing of risks.
• Insurance vs Assurance: Insurance = UNCERTAIN events (fire, accident). Assurance = CERTAIN events (death WILL happen; only when is uncertain). Life policies use the term Assurance.
• Pure Risk vs Speculative Risk: Pure Risk = only two outcomes — LOSS or NO LOSS. INSURABLE. Speculative Risk = profit, loss, or break-even (gambling). NOT insurable.
• IRDAI: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India. Established by IRDAI Act 1999. HQ: Hyderabad. Regulates all insurers and intermediaries; protects policyholder interests.
• LIC: Life Insurance Corporation of India formed in 1956 by nationalizing 245 private insurance companies. Remained the only life insurer until market liberalization in 2000.
• Peril vs Hazard: Peril = DIRECT cause of loss (fire, flood, earthquake). Hazard = condition that INCREASES the chance of a peril occurring (wet floor, faulty wiring).

🎯 HIGHLY REPEATED EXAM Q&A:
Q: Insurance originated in which place?
A) London  B) Rome  C) Rhodes, Greece  D) India
A: Rhodes, Greece

Q: IRDAI headquarters is located in?
A) Mumbai  B) Delhi  C) Hyderabad  D) Chennai
A: Hyderabad

Q: LIC was formed by nationalizing how many companies?
A) 100  B) 145  C) 245  D) 300
A: 245

Q: Which risk is INSURABLE?
A) Speculative Risk  B) Pure Risk  C) Both  D) Neither
A: Pure Risk

Q: Life insurance uses the term Assurance because death is:
A) Uncertain  B) Accidental  C) Preventable  D) Certain
A: Certain

items.title: Chapter 2: Core Elements of Insurance
items.description:
• Asset and Risk: Insurance applies only to assets with ECONOMIC VALUE facing genuine risk. No asset value or no risk = no insurable interest.
• Peril vs Hazard: Peril = DIRECT cause of loss (fire, flood). Hazard = condition that INCREASES likelihood of a peril occurring.
• Physical Hazard: A PHYSICAL condition increasing risk — poor health, unsafe building, obesity, wet floor. Visible and measurable.
• Moral Hazard: DISHONEST tendency to cause or exaggerate loss for financial gain — deliberate arson to claim insurance, inflating a claim.
• Morale Hazard: CARELESSNESS caused by having insurance — not locking car because it is insured, ignoring fire safety because property is insured.
• Law of Large Numbers: The LARGER the pool of similar risks, the more ACCURATELY future losses can be predicted. This is the statistical foundation of insurance pricing.
• Fundamental vs Particular Risk: Fundamental Risk = affects LARGE GROUPS simultaneously (earthquake, flood, pandemic). Particular Risk = affects INDIVIDUALS (house fire, car accident).
• Requirements for Insurable Risk: Large pool of similar exposures, accidental and unintentional loss, loss must be definite and measurable, must not be catastrophic to the insurer.

🎯 HIGHLY REPEATED EXAM Q&A:
Q: Deliberately burning a shop to claim insurance is an example of:
A) Physical Hazard  B) Moral Hazard  C) Morale Hazard  D) Peril
A: Moral Hazard

Q: Not locking your car because it is insured is:
A) Moral Hazard  B) Physical Hazard  C) Morale Hazard  D) Peril
A: Morale Hazard

Q: Law of Large Numbers states that:
A) Bigger claims paid faster  B) More policyholders = more accurate loss prediction  C) Premium rises with age  D) All risks are equal
A: More policyholders = more accurate loss prediction

Q: Earthquake affecting thousands of people is an example of:
A) Particular Risk  B) Pure Risk  C) Fundamental Risk  D) Speculative Risk
A: Fundamental Risk

Q: Fire causing loss to a house is an example of:
A) Peril  B) Hazard  C) Moral Hazard  D) Speculative Risk
A: Peril

items.title: Chapter 3: Principles of Insurance
items.description:
• Utmost Good Faith (Uberrima Fides): BOTH insurer and insured MUST disclose all MATERIAL FACTS honestly. Non-disclosure or misrepresentation makes the contract VOIDABLE. MOST IMPORTANT principle.
• Insurable Interest: Insured must have a FINANCIAL STAKE in the subject matter. In LIFE insurance: must exist at INCEPTION. In GENERAL insurance: must exist at CLAIM time.
• Indemnity: Insured restored to SAME financial position as before loss — NO PROFIT. Applies strictly to General Insurance. Life Insurance does NOT strictly follow indemnity.
• Subrogation: After paying the claim, insurer gets the RIGHT to SUE the responsible third party. Follows indemnity — does NOT apply to Life Insurance.
• Contribution: When MULTIPLE INSURERS cover the SAME RISK, they share the claim proportionally. Prevents insured from profiting by claiming from each insurer. Applies to General Insurance only.
• Proximate Cause: The IMMEDIATE, DIRECT, and DOMINANT cause of loss. Insured peril as proximate cause = claim PAID. Excluded peril as proximate cause = claim REJECTED.
• Loss Minimization: After a peril occurs, insured MUST take reasonable steps to MINIMIZE the loss (e.g., call fire brigade). Cannot claim extra damage due to own post-loss negligence.
• Insurable Interest in Life: SELF (unlimited). Spouse (mutual). Employer in key employee (Keyman). Creditor in debtor (up to debt amount).

🎯 HIGHLY REPEATED EXAM Q&A:
Q: Uberrima Fides means:
A) Insurable Interest  B) Utmost Good Faith  C) Indemnity  D) Subrogation
A: Utmost Good Faith

Q: Insurer pays motor accident claim, then sues the at-fault driver. This is:
A) Contribution  B) Indemnity  C) Subrogation  D) Good Faith
A: Subrogation

Q: In Life Insurance, insurable interest must exist at:
A) Claim time  B) Inception (time of policy)  C) Both  D) Neither
A: Inception

Q: Two insurers share a loss proportionately. This is the principle of:
A) Subrogation  B) Contribution  C) Indemnity  D) Good Faith
A: Contribution

Q: Principle of Indemnity does NOT strictly apply to:
A) Fire Insurance  B) Marine Insurance  C) Life Insurance  D) Motor Insurance
A: Life Insurance

items.title: Chapter 4: Features of Insurance Contracts
items.description:
• Valid Contract Elements: Offer, Acceptance, Consideration (PREMIUM), Competent parties (sound mind, not minor), Legal object, Free consent — all MUST be present.
• Aleatory Contract: Value exchanged is UNEQUAL and depends on a FUTURE UNCERTAIN EVENT. Insurer may pay far more than premium received, or pay nothing at all.
• Contract of Adhesion: Policy is PRINTED by insurer — insured must accept as-is, NO negotiation. Any AMBIGUITY interpreted in FAVOR OF THE INSURED (Contra Proferentem rule).
• Unilateral Contract: Only ONE party (the INSURER) makes a legally enforceable promise. Insured is NOT legally bound to pay premium — but policy lapses if not paid.
• Conditional Contract: Insurer's obligation to pay is CONDITIONAL on insured fulfilling conditions: paying premium, filing claim on time, adhering to policy conditions.
• Personal Contract: Between insurer and SPECIFIC INSURED. CANNOT be transferred to another without insurer's written consent.
• Wagering vs Insurance: Both involve uncertainty, BUT insurance requires insurable interest and compensates ACTUAL LOSS. Wagering CREATES risk; insurance COVERS pre-existing risk.
• Offer and Acceptance: Proposal Form = Offer by proposer. Acceptance = by Insurer after underwriting. Premium = Consideration. These three form the binding contract.

🎯 HIGHLY REPEATED EXAM Q&A:
Q: In insurance, the proposal form is filled by:
A) Insurer  B) Agent  C) Proposer/Applicant  D) IRDAI
A: Proposer/Applicant

Q: Any ambiguity in an insurance policy is interpreted in favor of:
A) Insurer  B) Agent  C) IRDAI  D) Insured
A: Insured

Q: An insurance contract where obligation depends on an uncertain event is called:
A) Unilateral  B) Aleatory  C) Bilateral  D) Wagering
A: Aleatory

Q: Insurance being a personal contract means:
A) Only individuals can buy  B) Cannot be assigned without consent  C) Families cannot share  D) Expires at death
A: Cannot be assigned without consent

Q: The consideration in an insurance contract is:
A) Proposal Form  B) Policy Document  C) Premium  D) Agent Commission
A: Premium

items.title: Chapter 5: Underwriting and Rating
items.description:
• Underwriting: Process of EVALUATING and SELECTING risks — deciding whether to insure and at what premium. The professional doing this is called an UNDERWRITER.
• Adverse Selection (Anti-Selection): Tendency for HIGH-RISK individuals to buy insurance disproportionately. Underwriting prevents this by properly assessing each risk.
• Risk Classification: STANDARD RISK = average risk, normal premium. SUB-STANDARD RISK = higher risk, extra premium charged. DECLINED RISK = too risky, policy NOT issued.
• Factors Affecting Life Premium: Age (older = higher), Gender (female = lower — longer life), Medical history, Occupation (hazardous = extra), Lifestyle (smoking/drinking), Sum Assured.
• Loading Types: DEBT LOADING = fixed extra amount per year. RATING-UP = treating proposer as older. EXCLUSION = excluding specific disease. LIEN = reduced benefit in early years.
• Group Underwriting: Done for the GROUP as a whole, not individuals. Medical examination generally NOT required above minimum group size.
• Free Cover Limit (FCL): In group policies, members covered up to a fixed amount without medical exam. Amount ABOVE FCL requires individual underwriting.
• Moral Hazard in Underwriting: Dishonest intent of proposer — deliberate misrepresentation, income mismatch, over-insurance attempt. If detected, policy may be declined.

🎯 HIGHLY REPEATED EXAM Q&A:
Q: The process of evaluating and selecting risks is called:
A) Actuarial Review  B) Underwriting  C) Claim Assessment  D) Nomination
A: Underwriting

Q: High-risk people buying insurance disproportionately is called:
A) Pure Risk  B) Loading  C) Adverse/Anti-Selection  D) Rebating
A: Adverse/Anti-Selection

Q: Person with diabetes is charged extra premium. This is called:
A) Bonus  B) Loading  C) Rebate  D) Surrender
A: Loading

Q: Treating a proposer as 5 years older due to health condition is called:
A) Debt Loading  B) Exclusion  C) Rating-Up  D) Decline
A: Rating-Up

Q: In group insurance, medical examination is generally:
A) Mandatory for all  B) Not required above certain group size  C) Required only for women  D) Done by IRDAI
A: Not required above certain group size

items.title: Chapter 6: Claims Processing
items.description:
• Claim: Formal request by insured/nominee to insurer for PAYMENT of policy benefit upon occurrence of the insured event. Claim is the primary reason insurance exists.
• Types of Life Claims: Maturity Claim (survives full term). Death Claim (dies during term). Survival/Money-back (periodic). Rider Claims (accident/disability). Annuity (pension payments).
• Death Claim Documents: Death Certificate (certified copy), Original Policy Bond, Form A (Claimant's Statement), Form B (Medical Attendant's Certificate), Form C (Hospital Certificate if hospitalized), Form E (Employer's Certificate), NEFT form, KYC.
• Early Claim: Death within 3 YEARS of policy issuance or revival. Insurer CAN INVESTIGATE for fraud, non-disclosure, or misrepresentation.
• Claim Settlement Timeline (IRDAI): Must SETTLE within 30 DAYS of receiving ALL DOCUMENTS. If investigation needed: must COMPLETE within 90 DAYS. Delayed payment = INTEREST payable.
• Repudiation: REJECTION of a claim. Grounds: non-disclosure, misrepresentation, policy lapsed, suicide within exclusion period, excluded cause, fraud.
• Suicide Clause: Insured commits suicide within 12 MONTHS (1 year) of policy issuance/revival = insurer pays ONLY PREMIUMS PAID, NOT full sum assured.
• Section 45: After 3 YEARS of policy, insurer CANNOT contest/repudiate on grounds of non-disclosure or misrepresentation UNLESS FRAUD is proven.

🎯 HIGHLY REPEATED EXAM Q&A:
Q: IRDAI mandates claim settlement within how many days of receiving all documents?
A) 15 days  B) 30 days  C) 60 days  D) 90 days
A: 30 days

Q: Death claim filed within 3 years of policy issuance is called:
A) Maturity Claim  B) Early Claim  C) Survival Claim  D) Rider Claim
A: Early Claim

Q: Insured commits suicide within 1 year of policy — insurer pays:
A) Full Sum Assured  B) Nothing  C) Only premiums paid  D) 50% of SA
A: Only premiums paid

Q: Rejection of an insurance claim is called:
A) Lapse  B) Forfeiture  C) Repudiation  D) Revival
A: Repudiation

Q: If investigation is needed in a death claim, it must be completed within:
A) 30 days  B) 60 days  C) 90 days  D) 120 days
A: 90 days

items.title: Chapter 7: Documentation
items.description:
• Proposal Form: The APPLICATION for insurance. Filled by the PROPOSER. It is the BASIS of the contract. Any incorrect/false information makes contract VOIDABLE.
• Prospectus: Document from INSURER describing the product — features, benefits, premium, exclusions, terms. Must be provided to customer BEFORE purchase.
• Policy Bond (Policy Document): Official LEGAL CONTRACT between insurer and insured. Contains policy number, SA, premium, term, riders, nominee details, exclusions, all terms.
• KYC Documents: Identity proof (Aadhaar, PAN, Passport), Address proof, Age proof (Birth Certificate, Passport, School TC), Income proof (for high sum assured).
• Free-Look Period: 15 DAYS from receipt of policy (normal). 30 DAYS for Distance Marketing (online/phone/direct mail). Refund = Premium MINUS proportionate risk premium MINUS medical charges.
• Assignment (Section 38): ABSOLUTE ASSIGNMENT = complete transfer of all rights; nominee rights SUSPENDED; insurer pays assignee. CONDITIONAL ASSIGNMENT = for loan security; reversed on repayment.
• Nomination (Section 39): Nominee receives death claim. Can be changed ANYTIME before death. Nominee = TRUSTEE for legal heirs, NOT the owner. Multiple nominees with % shares allowed.
• Revival: Lapsed policy revived within 5 YEARS from first unpaid premium. Requires all dues + interest + Declaration of Good Health (DGH). Medical exam if > 2 years lapsed.

🎯 HIGHLY REPEATED EXAM Q&A:
Q: Free Look Period for a policy sold online (Distance Marketing) is:
A) 10 days  B) 15 days  C) 30 days  D) 45 days
A: 30 days

Q: Nomination in Life Insurance is governed by Section:
A) 38  B) 39  C) 45  D) 64
A: Section 39

Q: Assignment in Life Insurance is governed by Section:
A) 38  B) 39  C) 45  D) 80C
A: Section 38

Q: A lapsed policy can be revived within how many years?
A) 2 years  B) 3 years  C) 5 years  D) 10 years
A: 5 years

Q: A nominee in life insurance is legally:
A) Owner of the policy  B) Trustee for legal heirs  C) Assignee  D) Co-insured
A: Trustee for legal heirs

items.title: Chapter 8: Customer Service
items.description:
• Grace Period: Extra time to pay overdue premium WITHOUT policy lapsing. YEARLY/HALF-YEARLY/QUARTERLY = 30 DAYS. MONTHLY = 15 DAYS. Death during grace period = CLAIM PAID (unpaid premium deducted from claim amount).
• Lapse: Policy loses all coverage when premium remains unpaid AFTER the grace period expires.
• Guaranteed Surrender Value (GSV): Payable when policy surrendered AFTER 3 YEARS. Usually 30% of total premiums paid (EXCLUDING 1st year premium and rider premiums).
• Special Surrender Value (SSV): Usually HIGHER than GSV. Based on paid-up value + accrued bonuses. Offered at insurer's discretion.
• Paid-Up Policy: If premiums stopped AFTER 3 YEARS, policy does NOT lapse — continues with REDUCED sum assured. Formula: Paid-Up SA = (Premiums Paid / Total Premiums Payable) x Original SA.
• Policy Loan: Available AFTER 3 YEARS. Loan up to 90% of SURRENDER VALUE. Interest charged. Policy assigned to insurer as security. Reversed on loan repayment.
• Revival/Reinstatement: Lapsed policy revived within 5 YEARS from first unpaid premium. Requires all dues + interest + DGH. Medical exam if lapsed > 2 years.
• Free-Look Refund: Premium paid MINUS proportionate risk premium MINUS medical exam charges returned if policy returned within free-look period (15 days normal / 30 days distance marketing).

🎯 HIGHLY REPEATED EXAM Q&A:
Q: Grace period for monthly mode premium payment is:
A) 7 days  B) 15 days  C) 30 days  D) 45 days
A: 15 days

Q: If an insured dies during the grace period, the insurer:
A) Rejects the claim  B) Pays claim minus outstanding premium  C) Pays only half the claim  D) Voids the policy
A: Pays claim minus outstanding premium

Q: Guaranteed Surrender Value is payable after how many policy years?
A) 1 year  B) 2 years  C) 3 years  D) 5 years
A: 3 years

Q: Policy continuing with reduced sum assured after stopping premiums is called:
A) Lapsed Policy  B) Surrendered Policy  C) Paid-Up Policy  D) Expired Policy
A: Paid-Up Policy

Q: Maximum policy loan amount is generally up to:
A) 50% of Sum Assured  B) 75% of Paid-Up Value  C) 90% of Surrender Value  D) 100% premiums paid
A: 90% of Surrender Value

items.title: Chapter 9: Grievance Redressal Mechanism (Ombudsman)
items.description:
• Grievance Hierarchy: Level 1 = Insurer's Internal Grievance Cell. Level 2 = Insurance Ombudsman. Level 3 = Consumer Court / Civil Court.
• Insurance Ombudsman: Established under Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017. Resolves policyholder disputes FREE OF COST and QUICKLY. 17 OMBUDSMAN OFFICES across India.
• Ombudsman Jurisdiction: Complaints up to Rs. 50 LAKHS. Complaints above Rs. 50 Lakhs must go to Civil/Consumer Court.
• What Ombudsman Handles: Claim rejection or delay, dispute on premium, policy not issued, mis-selling, dispute on policy terms.
• Pre-condition to Approach: Must FIRST complain to insurer. Can approach Ombudsman ONLY IF: (a) received insurer's final reply, OR (b) no reply within 30 DAYS. Must file within 1 YEAR of insurer's final reply.
• Award Timeline: Ombudsman must pass award within 3 MONTHS of receiving complete complaint. Award is binding on insurer; policyholder may accept or reject.
• IGMS: Integrated Grievance Management System — IRDAI's online portal (igms.irda.gov.in) for registering and tracking complaints.
• Insurer Internal TAT: Acknowledge complaint within 3 WORKING DAYS. Resolve within 15 DAYS (IRDAI norm). If unresolved, policyholder can approach Ombudsman.

🎯 HIGHLY REPEATED EXAM Q&A:
Q: Maximum claim amount Insurance Ombudsman can handle is:
A) Rs. 20 Lakhs  B) Rs. 30 Lakhs  C) Rs. 50 Lakhs  D) Rs. 1 Crore
A: Rs. 50 Lakhs

Q: Insurance Ombudsman must pass an award within:
A) 1 month  B) 2 months  C) 3 months  D) 6 months
A: 3 months

Q: Before approaching Ombudsman, the complainant must have:
A) Paid all premiums  B) Filed complaint with insurer first  C) Hired a lawyer  D) Paid fees
A: Filed complaint with insurer first

Q: How many Insurance Ombudsman offices are there in India?
A) 8  B) 12  C) 17  D) 25
A: 17

Q: IGMS stands for:
A) Insurance General Management System  B) Integrated Grievance Management System  C) Indian Grievance Monitoring System  D) Insurance Grievance Mediation System
A: Integrated Grievance Management System

items.title: Chapter 10: Regulatory Aspects for Insurance Agents
items.description:
• IRDAI: Established by IRDAI Act 1999. HQ: Hyderabad. Regulates all insurers and intermediaries; promotes insurance; protects policyholders.
• Insurance Agent: Appointed by INSURER to solicit insurance. Agent LEGALLY REPRESENTS the INSURER (not the customer). Earns commission on premium.
• Agent License: Must pass IRDAI prescribed exam (IC-38 for life insurance). Must complete MINIMUM 50 HOURS of pre-licensing training. License MANDATORY before selling.
• License Renewal: Every 3 YEARS. Must complete minimum 25 HOURS of Continuing Education (CE) in each 3-year block.
• Rebating (ILLEGAL): Offering any part of commission or benefit as inducement to buy insurance. Prohibited under Section 41 of Insurance Act. BOTH agent and customer can be penalized.
• Code of Conduct: Must NOT misrepresent policy terms. Must NOT suppress material facts. Must NOT induce needless policy switching for commission (CHURNING). Must NOT sell unsuitable products.
• Commission Structure: First Year Commission (FYC) is HIGHER than Renewal Commission. Rates set by IRDAI. Commission CANNOT be paid to unlicensed persons.
• Types of Intermediaries: Individual Agent. Corporate Agent (bank/NBFC). Broker (represents buyer). Web Aggregator (online comparison). POSP (Point of Sale Person).

🎯 HIGHLY REPEATED EXAM Q&A:
Q: An insurance agent is appointed by:
A) IRDAI  B) Customer  C) Insurer  D) Government
A: Insurer

Q: Agent license must be renewed every:
A) 1 year  B) 2 years  C) 3 years  D) 5 years
A: 3 years

Q: Sharing commission with customer as inducement to buy a policy is called:
A) Bonus  B) Rebating  C) Loading  D) Discount
A: Rebating

Q: Pre-licensing training for insurance agents requires a minimum of:
A) 25 hours  B) 35 hours  C) 50 hours  D) 100 hours
A: 50 hours

Q: An insurance agent legally represents:
A) The policyholder  B) The insurer  C) IRDAI  D) The court
A: The insurer

items.title: Chapter 11: What Life Insurance Involves
items.description:
• Definition: A contract where the insurer pays Sum Assured to nominee/policyholder on the insured's DEATH during term OR SURVIVAL to maturity, in exchange for regular premiums.
• Key Parties: Insurer (company). Life Assured/Insured (person covered). Proposer/Policyholder (pays premium; may differ from insured). Nominee (receives death benefit). Beneficiary (ultimate recipient).
• Human Life Value (HLV): Economic value of a person's future income stream. Used to determine ADEQUATE insurance coverage. HLV = (Annual Income - Personal Expenses) x Remaining Working Years.
• IALM: Indian Assured Lives Mortality table — used by actuaries to calculate MORTALITY RATES for pricing Indian life insurance products.
• Premium Components: Mortality Charge (cost of death cover) + Expense Loading (admin/commission) + Investment Return component = GROSS PREMIUM (what policyholder pays).
• Insurable Interest in Life: SELF (unlimited). Spouse (mutual, unlimited). Employer in key employee (Keyman). Creditor in debtor (up to debt amount).
• Primary Purpose: Life insurance is PROTECTION against financial hardship from premature death. NOT primarily savings or investment — protection comes first.
• Surrender vs Lapse: SURRENDER = voluntary cancellation (gets surrender value after 3 years). LAPSE = involuntary; policy stops due to non-payment of premium.

🎯 HIGHLY REPEATED EXAM Q&A:
Q: The person whose life is covered in a life insurance policy is called:
A) Proposer  B) Insurer  C) Life Assured / Insured  D) Nominee
A: Life Assured / Insured

Q: HLV stands for:
A) High Level Value  B) Human Life Value  C) Health Life Value  D) Historic Loss Value
A: Human Life Value

Q: IALM is used by actuaries to calculate:
A) Tax liability  B) Surrender Value  C) Mortality Rate  D) Bonus
A: Mortality Rate

Q: The PRIMARY purpose of life insurance is:
A) Investment  B) Tax saving  C) Protection against financial loss  D) Retirement planning
A: Protection against financial loss

Q: A person can buy life insurance on another person's life only if:
A) They are related  B) Insurable interest exists  C) Age above 18  D) Insurer approves
A: Insurable interest exists

items.title: Chapter 12: Financial Planning
items.description:
• Financial Planning: Meeting life goals through proper management of income, expenses, savings, investments, and insurance — tailored to each stage of life.
• Life Stages and Insurance Needs: Young Single = start savings, LOW insurance. Young Married = HIGH protection needed. Married with Children = MAXIMUM protection + education plan. Pre-Retirement = wealth accumulation. Retirement = annuity/pension/health coverage.
• Financial Goals: SHORT-TERM (1-3 yrs) = vacation, gadgets. MEDIUM-TERM (3-5 yrs) = car, home renovation. LONG-TERM (5+ yrs) = home, children's education, retirement.
• Risk Pyramid: BASE = Low Risk (LIC, PPF, FD). MIDDLE = Medium Risk (Mutual Funds, Debt). TOP = High Risk (Equity, stocks). Life insurance sits at the BASE.
• Tax Benefits: Premium up to Rs. 1.5 LAKHS/year deductible under SECTION 80C. Death and maturity proceeds tax-exempt under SECTION 10(10D). Health insurance premium under SECTION 80D (Rs. 25,000 self/family; Rs. 50,000 senior citizens).
• Emergency Fund: Maintain 3-6 months of expenses as liquid reserve. Insurance supplements but does NOT replace emergency savings.
• Power of Compounding: Starting early dramatically improves long-term wealth and coverage. Time in market beats timing the market.
• Inflation Protection: Fixed coverage loses real value over time. ULIPs, bonus-linked plans, and increasing term plans help hedge against inflation.

🎯 HIGHLY REPEATED EXAM Q&A:
Q: Life insurance premium is tax deductible under:
A) Section 80D  B) Section 80C  C) Section 10(10D)  D) Section 24
A: Section 80C

Q: Death and maturity proceeds of life insurance are tax-free under:
A) Section 80C  B) Section 80D  C) Section 10(10D)  D) Section 54
A: Section 10(10D)

Q: Maximum deduction under Section 80C for life insurance premium is:
A) Rs. 50,000  B) Rs. 1 Lakh  C) Rs. 1.5 Lakhs  D) Rs. 2 Lakhs
A: Rs. 1.5 Lakhs

Q: In the financial risk pyramid, life insurance is placed at:
A) Top (High Risk)  B) Middle  C) Base (Low Risk)  D) Outside the pyramid
A: Base (Low Risk)

Q: For a young married person with a new family, the MOST important financial need is:
A) High savings  B) High protection / life cover  C) Equity investments  D) Fixed deposits
A: High protection / life cover

items.title: Chapter 13: Life Insurance Products – Traditional
items.description:
• Term Insurance: PURE PROTECTION ONLY. Pays Sum Assured ONLY on death within policy term. NO maturity benefit. LOWEST premium. Best for maximum protection at minimum cost.
• Endowment Policy: PROTECTION + SAVINGS combo. Pays SA on DEATH or at MATURITY — whichever occurs FIRST. Higher premium. Bonuses added. Most popular traditional plan.
• Whole Life Policy: Covers entire life (typically up to age 100). Death benefit whenever death occurs. Ideal for ESTATE PLANNING and leaving wealth for heirs.
• Money-Back Policy: Pays % of SA at REGULAR INTERVALS during term (survival benefits). BALANCE + BONUS paid at maturity. Provides periodic LIQUIDITY during policy term.
• Jeevan Anand (LIC): Endowment + Whole Life combination. SA + Bonus paid at MATURITY. Policy CONTINUES as whole life cover after maturity at no extra premium.
• Annuity / Pension Plans: Accumulation phase then regular income. IMMEDIATE ANNUITY = payments start right after lump sum. DEFERRED ANNUITY = accumulate first, annuity starts at a future date.
• Children's Plans: Build corpus for child's education/marriage. PREMIUM WAIVER BENEFIT = if parent dies, insurer pays future premiums; policy continues.
• Bonus Types: SIMPLE REVERSIONARY BONUS = % of SA added yearly. COMPOUND REVERSIONARY = % of (SA + accrued bonus). TERMINAL BONUS = extra, paid ONLY at maturity or death claim.

🎯 HIGHLY REPEATED EXAM Q&A:
Q: Which life insurance plan has NO maturity benefit?
A) Endowment  B) Whole Life  C) Term Insurance  D) Money-Back
A: Term Insurance

Q: A plan that pays survival benefits periodically AND balance at maturity is:
A) Term Plan  B) Whole Life  C) Endowment  D) Money-Back Plan
A: Money-Back Plan

Q: Endowment plan pays Sum Assured:
A) Only on death  B) Only at maturity  C) On death OR maturity, whichever is earlier  D) Only on survival
A: On death OR maturity, whichever is earlier

Q: Which plan is best for estate planning (leaving wealth for heirs)?
A) Term Insurance  B) Whole Life Policy  C) Money-Back  D) ULIP
A: Whole Life Policy

Q: Annuity payments starting immediately after a lump sum payment is called:
A) Deferred Annuity  B) Immediate Annuity  C) Pension Annuity  D) Whole Life Annuity
A: Immediate Annuity

items.title: Chapter 14: Life Insurance Products – Non-Traditional (ULIPs)
items.description:
• ULIP = Unit Linked Insurance Plan: Combines LIFE INSURANCE + MARKET-LINKED INVESTMENT. Premium split: part = life cover (mortality charge), part = invested in market-linked funds.
• Fund Options: EQUITY FUND (high risk/return, stocks). DEBT FUND (low risk/return, bonds/gilt). BALANCED FUND (mix). MONEY MARKET FUND (very low risk, liquid). Policyholder CHOOSES and can SWITCH.
• NAV (Net Asset Value): Price per UNIT of a ULIP fund. Units allotted = Investment Amount / NAV. Investment value = Units held x Current NAV. NAV changes DAILY.
• Lock-in Period: MANDATORY 5 YEARS as per IRDAI 2010 guidelines. NO withdrawals in first 5 years. Partial withdrawals allowed AFTER 5 years.
• ULIP Charges: Premium Allocation Charge (upfront, before investing). Mortality Charge (monthly, cost of life cover). Fund Management Charge (FMC) = MAX 1.35% per annum. Policy Administration Charge. Surrender Charge (minimal post-2010 reforms).
• IRDAI 2010 ULIP Reforms: Min SA = 10x annual premium (age < 45) or 7x (age >= 45). 5-year mandatory lock-in. Cap on charges. Minimum 5-year policy term.
• Switching: Moving allocation between funds (equity to debt to reduce risk). Limited FREE SWITCHES per year; charges apply after free limit.
• ULIP vs Traditional: ULIP = market-linked, transparent, flexible, higher risk. Traditional = guaranteed/bonus returns, stable, lower risk, less transparent.

🎯 HIGHLY REPEATED EXAM Q&A:
Q: Minimum lock-in period for a ULIP is:
A) 1 year  B) 3 years  C) 5 years  D) 7 years
A: 5 years

Q: NAV in ULIP stands for:
A) Net Annual Value  B) Net Asset Value  C) New Allocation Value  D) Normal Asset Valuation
A: Net Asset Value

Q: Maximum Fund Management Charge (FMC) allowed in ULIP is:
A) 0.5%  B) 1%  C) 1.35%  D) 2%
A: 1.35%

Q: For ULIP by a person below 45 years, minimum Sum Assured must be:
A) 5x  B) 7x  C) 10x  D) 15x annual premium
A: 10x annual premium

Q: In a ULIP, moving money from one fund to another is called:
A) Revival  B) Partial Withdrawal  C) Switching  D) Surrender
A: Switching

items.title: Chapter 15: Applications of Life Insurance (MWP Act, Keyman Insurance)
items.description:
• MWP Act 1874 — Section 6: A MARRIED MAN can buy a life policy for the benefit of his WIFE and/or CHILDREN. Creates an AUTOMATIC TRUST. Proceeds PROTECTED from creditors and husband's debts.
• MWP Act — Critical Rules: Only a MARRIED MAN can take this policy (not a woman). Endorsed at INCEPTION ONLY — CANNOT be added later. CANNOT be ASSIGNED, SURRENDERED, or claimed by the husband — EVER.
• Keyman Insurance: Business takes insurance on life of a KEY EMPLOYEE (founder, director, key salesperson). Purpose: compensate BUSINESS for financial loss if that key person dies.
• Keyman — Tax Treatment: Premium paid by COMPANY = TAX DEDUCTIBLE as business expense. Company = policyholder AND beneficiary. Death benefit received by company = TAXABLE in company's hands.
• Group Life Insurance: One MASTER POLICY covers a group (employees, association members). Certificate issued to each member. Low cost. Employer usually pays premium.
• Salary Saving Scheme (SSS): Employer DEDUCTS premium from employee salary and remits to insurer. Ensures timely payment; convenient for employees.
• Joint Life Policy: Covers TWO lives (husband-wife or business partners). Death benefit paid on the FIRST DEATH. Surviving person receives the benefit.
• Assignment for Loan: Policy ASSIGNED to lender as collateral when loan is taken. On FULL REPAYMENT of loan, assignment is REVERSED.

🎯 HIGHLY REPEATED EXAM Q&A:
Q: Under MWP Act, who can take a policy to protect wife and children?
A) Any man  B) Only unmarried man  C) Only married man  D) Any woman
A: Only married man

Q: A MWP Act policy can be assigned by the husband:
A) Anytime  B) After 5 years  C) Only at inception  D) NEVER — it cannot be assigned
A: NEVER — it cannot be assigned

Q: In Keyman Insurance, the premium is paid by:
A) The key employee  B) IRDAI  C) The company / employer  D) Government
A: The company / employer

Q: In Keyman Insurance, the death benefit is received by:
A) Family of key employee  B) The company  C) Government  D) Employees union
A: The company

Q: Under MWP Act, the policy proceeds are protected from:
A) Income Tax  B) Creditors and husband's debts  C) Nominee's claims  D) IRDAI regulations
A: Creditors and husband's debts

items.title: Chapter 16: Pricing and Valuation in Life Insurance
items.description:
• Premium: Price paid by policyholder for coverage. Modes: Yearly (cheapest), Half-yearly, Quarterly, Monthly. Yearly mode attracts a discount due to early receipt of funds.
• Net Premium vs Gross Premium: NET PREMIUM = pure cost of risk (mortality + savings). GROSS PREMIUM = Net Premium + Expense Loading (admin, commission). Policyholder pays GROSS PREMIUM.
• Factors Affecting Life Premium: Age (older = higher). Gender (female = lower — live longer). Sum Assured (higher = higher). Occupation (hazardous = extra). Habits (smoking = extra). Policy term.
• IALM: Indian Assured Lives Mortality table used by actuaries. Gives probability of death at each age for Indian lives. Higher mortality = higher mortality charge.
• Bonus Types: SIMPLE REVERSIONARY = fixed % of SA added yearly. COMPOUND REVERSIONARY = % of (SA + accrued bonus). TERMINAL BONUS = extra, paid ONLY at maturity or death claim.
• Actuarial Valuation: Periodic (at least yearly) assessment by a QUALIFIED ACTUARY to ensure insurer has ADEQUATE RESERVES to pay all future claims.
• Reserve: Funds set aside by insurer for FUTURE CLAIM OBLIGATIONS. Under-reserving = insurer cannot pay claims. IRDAI mandates minimum reserve levels.
• Solvency Margin: Minimum excess of assets over liabilities. IRDAI requires minimum SOLVENCY RATIO of 1.5 (150%).

🎯 HIGHLY REPEATED EXAM Q&A:
Q: Gross Premium = Net Premium + ?
A) Sum Assured  B) Bonus  C) Expense Loading  D) Surrender Value
A: Expense Loading

Q: Mortality table used for Indian lives in life insurance pricing is:
A) LIC Mortality Table  B) IRDA Table  C) IALM  D) CSO Table
A: IALM (Indian Assured Lives Mortality)

Q: Professional who calculates premiums and ensures financial soundness of insurer:
A) Underwriter  B) Agent  C) Actuary  D) Claims Manager
A: Actuary

Q: IRDAI requires insurers to maintain a minimum solvency ratio of:
A) 1.0  B) 1.25  C) 1.5  D) 2.0
A: 1.5

Q: Bonus declared as a percentage of Sum Assured every year is called:
A) Terminal Bonus  B) Compound Reversionary Bonus  C) Simple Reversionary Bonus  D) Loyalty Bonus
A: Simple Reversionary Bonus

items.title: Chapter 17: Life Insurance Documentation
items.description:
• Proposal Form: Application for life insurance. Filled by PROPOSER. Basis of the contract. Contains health declaration, habits, occupation, existing policies, income. False information = policy VOIDABLE.
• Age Proof — Standard: Birth Certificate, School/College Certificate (TC), Passport, PAN Card. Non-Standard: Ration Card, Horoscope, Affidavit (insurer's discretion).
• Medical Examination: Required when SA exceeds Non-Medical Limit (NML) or proposer above certain age. Done by INSURER-EMPANELED DOCTOR. Report forms part of proposal.
• Policy Bond: Official legal contract. Contains policy no., SA, premium, term, mode, riders, nominee, exclusions, and all conditions. Must be carefully preserved.
• Nomination (Section 39): Nominee receives claim on death. Can be changed ANYTIME. Nominee = TRUSTEE for legal heirs. Multiple nominees allowed with % shares.
• Assignment (Section 38): ABSOLUTE = complete transfer; nominee rights SUSPENDED; insurer pays assignee. CONDITIONAL = for loan; reversed on repayment.
• Revival Documents: DGH (Declaration of Good Health) form + all dues + interest. Medical exam if lapsed > 2 YEARS. Revival window = 5 YEARS from first unpaid premium.
• Distance Marketing: Sold online/phone/direct mail. FREE LOOK PERIOD = 30 DAYS. All terms must be prominently disclosed at time of sale.

🎯 HIGHLY REPEATED EXAM Q&A:
Q: Nomination in life insurance is governed by Section:
A) 38  B) 39  C) 45  D) 64
A: Section 39

Q: Assignment in life insurance is governed by Section:
A) 38  B) 39  C) 45  D) 80C
A: Section 38

Q: Which is a STANDARD age proof for life insurance?
A) Horoscope  B) Ration Card  C) Passport  D) Self-declaration
A: Passport

Q: On absolute assignment, the nominee's rights are:
A) Doubled  B) Unchanged  C) Suspended — insurer pays assignee  D) Transferred to nominee's children
A: Suspended — insurer pays assignee

Q: Free look period for policies sold via phone or internet is:
A) 10 days  B) 15 days  C) 30 days  D) 45 days
A: 30 days

items.title: Chapter 18: Life Insurance Underwriting
items.description:
• Underwriting Outcomes: ACCEPT at standard rate. ACCEPT with EXTRA PREMIUM. ACCEPT with EXCLUSIONS. POSTPONE (reapply later). DECLINE (refuse to insure).
• Medical Underwriting: Assesses health condition via medical exams, health reports, APR. Required when SA exceeds Non-Medical Limit (NML) or proposer is above age threshold.
• Non-Medical (NM) Underwriting: Below NML, NO medical exam required. Policy accepted based on Declaration of Good Health in proposal form. Faster and cost-effective.
• Financial Underwriting: SA must be proportional to INCOME/ASSETS. Prevents OVER-INSURANCE (moral hazard). Documents: Salary slip, ITR, Bank statement.
• Special Reports: APR = Attending Physician's Report (doctor's health assessment). ACR = Agent's Confidential Report (agent's view of proposer's habits, character, lifestyle). Employer's Certificate (income and occupation verification).
• Section 45 Protection: After 3 YEARS of policy inception, insurer CANNOT contest or repudiate on grounds of non-disclosure or misrepresentation — UNLESS FRAUD is proven.
• Extra Premium Loading Methods: DEBT LOADING (flat extra per year). RATING-UP (treating as older). EXCLUSION (specific condition excluded). INCREASING DEBT (extra increases with age).
• Juvenile / Minor Underwriting: Life insurance on child's life. Parent's health may also be assessed. SA during minority typically CAPPED. VESTING CLAUSE applies when child becomes adult.

🎯 HIGHLY REPEATED EXAM Q&A:
Q: After how many years can insurer NOT contest a policy under Section 45?
A) 1 year  B) 2 years  C) 3 years  D) 5 years
A: 3 years

Q: Agent's Confidential Report (ACR) provides:
A) Insurer's financial status  B) Agent's assessment of proposer's habits and character  C) AML compliance details  D) Medical examination results
A: Agent's assessment of proposer's habits and character

Q: Proposer with high BP treated as 5 years older for premium calculation:
A) Decline  B) Debt Loading  C) Rating-Up  D) Exclusion
A: Rating-Up

Q: Financial underwriting is done to prevent:
A) Adverse selection  B) Over-insurance and moral hazard  C) Early death claims  D) Policy lapse
A: Over-insurance and moral hazard

Q: APR stands for:
A) Annual Premium Receipt  B) Attending Physician's Report  C) Agent Premium Record  D) Actuarial Premium Rating
A: Attending Physician's Report

items.title: Chapter 19: Life Insurance Claims
items.description:
• Types of Life Claims: MATURITY (survives full term). DEATH (dies during term). RIDER (accident/disability). SURVIVAL / MONEY-BACK (periodic payouts). ANNUITY (pension installments).
• Maturity Claim Documents: Original Policy Bond, Signed Discharge Voucher, NEFT form, Identity/address proof, Age proof (if not admitted earlier).
• Death Claim Documents: Policy Bond, Death Certificate (certified copy), Form A (Claimant's Statement), Form B (Medical Attendant's Certificate), Form C (Hospital Certificate if hospitalized), Form E (Employer's Certificate), NEFT form, KYC.
• Early Claim Investigation: Death within 3 YEARS of issuance or revival = EARLY CLAIM. INVESTIGATION mandatory. Insurer can probe fraud, non-disclosure, misrepresentation.
• IRDAI Claim Timelines: All documents received — settle within 30 DAYS. If investigation needed — complete within 90 DAYS. Delayed payment = INTEREST payable.
• Presumption of Death: Person missing for 7 YEARS — Court declares legally dead under Section 108 of Indian Evidence Act. Death claim payable after court order.
• Section 45 (3-year protection): Policy over 3 years old — insurer CANNOT contest on misrepresentation unless FRAUD proven. Strong protection for nominee.
• Nomination Priority: Alive nominee — claim paid to nominee. Nominee predeceased insured with no fresh nomination — paid to LEGAL HEIRS.

🎯 HIGHLY REPEATED EXAM Q&A:
Q: IRDAI mandates claim settlement within how many days of receiving all documents?
A) 15 days  B) 30 days  C) 60 days  D) 90 days
A: 30 days

Q: A missing person can be declared legally dead after being missing for:
A) 3 years  B) 5 years  C) 7 years  D) 10 years
A: 7 years

Q: Form B (Medical Attendant's Certificate) is required in:
A) Maturity Claim  B) Death Claim  C) Survival Claim  D) Annuity Claim
A: Death Claim

Q: If investigation is needed in a death claim, it must be completed within:
A) 30 days  B) 60 days  C) 90 days  D) 120 days
A: 90 days

Q: A claim arising from death within first 3 years of policy is called:
A) Maturity Claim  B) Late Claim  C) Early Claim  D) Rider Claim
A: Early Claim

items.title: Chapter 20: Introduction to Health Insurance
items.description:
• Health Insurance: Covers medical expenses due to illness or injury. Covers hospitalization (min 24 hrs), day-care, pre/post hospitalization. Can be INDEMNITY (reimburse actual) or BENEFIT (lump sum on diagnosis).
• Types: Individual (one person). Family Floater (shared SA for entire family). Group Health (employer-employee). Critical Illness (lump sum on diagnosis). PA (accident only).
• IRDAI Health Insurance Regulations 2016: LIFETIME RENEWABILITY mandatory. PORTABILITY right. Standard exclusions across all policies. Standardized definitions.
• TPA (Third Party Administrator): Licensed intermediary managing cashless claims, hospital network, card issuance, claim processing. Registered with IRDAI. TPA CANNOT bear financial risk.
• Waiting Periods: INITIAL WAITING PERIOD = 30 DAYS (no claims except accident). SPECIFIC DISEASE WAITING = 1-2 YEARS (cataract, hernia). PED WAITING = 48 MONTHS (3-4 years).
• Pre-Existing Disease (PED): Any condition/illness EXISTING BEFORE buying the policy. Must be FULLY DISCLOSED at proposal. Standard waiting period: 48 MONTHS.
• Portability: Move health policy from one insurer to another at renewal WITHOUT LOSING waiting period credit already served. IRDAI mandated from 2011.
• Indemnity vs Benefit: INDEMNITY = reimburses ACTUAL EXPENSES (Mediclaim). BENEFIT = pays FIXED AMOUNT on diagnosis regardless of actual expenses (Critical Illness, PA).

🎯 HIGHLY REPEATED EXAM Q&A:
Q: TPA stands for:
A) Third Party Agency  B) Third Party Administrator  C) Total Premium Amount  D) Treatment Provision Authority
A: Third Party Administrator

Q: Standard waiting period for Pre-existing Diseases in health insurance is:
A) 1 year  B) 2 years  C) 30 days  D) 48 months (3-4 years)
A: 48 months (3-4 years)

Q: In a Family Floater policy, the sum insured is:
A) Separate for each member  B) Shared by entire family  C) Only for policyholder  D) Fixed per disease
A: Shared by entire family

Q: Initial waiting period in health insurance (no claims except accident) is:
A) 15 days  B) 30 days  C) 45 days  D) 60 days
A: 30 days

Q: Portability in health insurance allows:
A) Changing sum insured  B) Adding family members  C) Switching insurer without losing waiting period credit  D) Canceling anytime
A: Switching insurer without losing waiting period credit

items.title: Chapter 21: Health Insurance Documentation
items.description:
• Proposal Form: Filled by proposer. Contains personal details, FULL medical history, lifestyle habits, existing insurance. MUST disclose ALL pre-existing conditions. Non-disclosure = CLAIM REPUDIATION.
• Policy Schedule: Main policy document. Shows policyholder name, covered members, sum insured, policy period, premium paid, network hospitals, and exclusions.
• Pre-Authorization (Pre-Auth): Required for CASHLESS hospitalization. Hospital sends to TPA BEFORE elective admission. For EMERGENCY: must send within 24 HOURS of admission. TPA approves based on policy.
• Claim Form: Required for reimbursement claims. Must be submitted within 30 DAYS of discharge (typically 30-90 days as per insurer). Duly signed by insured.
• Cashless Claim Documents: Pre-auth approval, Hospital admission records, Doctor's prescription, Final hospital bill, Discharge summary, Lab/X-ray reports, Pharmacy bills.
• Reimbursement Claim Documents: Filled Claim Form, ALL ORIGINAL bills and receipts, Doctor's prescription, Discharge summary, Investigation reports, FIR (accident), Death Certificate (if died during hospitalization).
• Health Card: Issued by insurer/TPA to EACH INSURED MEMBER. Used for cashless treatment at NETWORK HOSPITALS. Contains policy number, TPA name, helpline, insured's name/photo.
• KYC in Health Insurance: PAN, Aadhaar, address proof, age proof (mandatory for seniors), recent photograph for health card.

🎯 HIGHLY REPEATED EXAM Q&A:
Q: For cashless elective surgery, pre-authorization must be sent to TPA:
A) After surgery  B) Before admission  C) Within 1 week  D) At time of billing
A: Before admission

Q: Document issued by TPA to each insured for cashless treatment is:
A) Discharge Summary  B) Health Card  C) Policy Bond  D) FIR
A: Health Card

Q: For emergency hospitalization, pre-auth must be sent to TPA within:
A) 6 hours  B) 12 hours  C) 24 hours  D) 48 hours
A: 24 hours

Q: Discharge summary is required for:
A) Only maturity claims  B) Both cashless and reimbursement claims  C) Only accident claims  D) Only critical illness claims
A: Both cashless and reimbursement claims

Q: Non-disclosure of a Pre-existing Disease in proposal can result in:
A) Lower premium  B) Bonus  C) Repudiation of claim  D) Policy upgrade
A: Repudiation of claim

items.title: Chapter 22: Health Insurance Products
items.description:
• Individual Health Insurance (Mediclaim): ONE PERSON covered. SA specific to that person. Covers in-patient hospitalization (min 24 HOURS), pre-hosp (30 DAYS before), post-hosp (60 DAYS after). Most basic health insurance form.
• Family Floater Policy: Entire family under ONE policy. Sum insured is SHARED. Premium based on ELDEST MEMBER's age. Cost-effective but risky if multiple claims in one year.
• Critical Illness (CI) Plan: LUMP SUM paid on DIAGNOSIS of specified critical illnesses (heart attack, cancer, stroke, kidney failure, bypass, major organ transplant). BENEFIT policy — NOT indemnity. No bills needed to claim.
• Personal Accident (PA) Policy: Covers accident-related: Death (100% SA), Permanent Total Disability (PTD = 100% SA), Permanent Partial Disability (PPD = % per schedule), Temporary Total Disability (TTD = weekly benefit).
• Top-up vs Super Top-up: TOP-UP = kicks in when SINGLE CLAIM exceeds the deductible. SUPER TOP-UP = kicks in when CUMULATIVE ANNUAL claims exceed the deductible. Both are cost-effective ways to increase health coverage affordably.
• Group Health Insurance: One MASTER POLICY covers all employees. Generally NO WAITING PERIOD for PED. Certificate issued to each employee. Employer pays premium.
• Senior Citizen Plans: For age 60+. Higher premium. CO-PAYMENT clause common (insured pays 10-20% of each claim). Keeps premium affordable.
• Standalone Health Insurers: Star Health, Niva Bupa (Max Bupa), Care Health (Religare), Aditya Birla Health Insurance — specialize ONLY in health insurance.

🎯 HIGHLY REPEATED EXAM Q&A:
Q: Critical Illness plan pays:
A) Based on actual expenses  B) Lump sum on diagnosis  C) Only on death  D) Monthly benefit
A: Lump sum on diagnosis

Q: In a Family Floater, premium is based on:
A) Youngest member's age  B) Average family age  C) Eldest member's age  D) Sum of all ages
A: Eldest member's age

Q: Permanent Total Disability (PTD) benefit in PA policy is:
A) 25% of SA  B) 50% of SA  C) 75% of SA  D) 100% of SA
A: 100% of SA

Q: Super Top-up plan works on a ___ basis for the deductible:
A) Per hospitalization  B) Per doctor visit  C) Cumulative annual  D) Per month
A: Cumulative annual

Q: In Group Health Insurance, Pre-existing Diseases are generally:
A) Never covered  B) Covered from day 1 (no waiting period)  C) Covered after 1 year  D) Covered after 3 years
A: Covered from day 1 (no waiting period)

items.title: Chapter 23: Health Insurance Underwriting
items.description:
• Health Underwriting: Assessing health risk before issuing a policy. Determines PREMIUM, EXCLUSIONS, or LOADINGS based on health profile. Ensures balanced risk pool and prevents adverse selection.
• Key Underwriting Factors: Age, Gender, BMI, Pre-existing conditions, Family medical history, Lifestyle (smoking/drinking), Occupation (hazardous = loading), Geographic location.
• BMI Classification: UNDERWEIGHT = below 18.5. NORMAL = 18.5 to 24.9. OVERWEIGHT = 25 to 29.9. OBESE = 30 and above. HIGH BMI = loading or exclusion.
• Waiting Periods Summary: Initial = 30 DAYS. Specific Disease = 1-2 YEARS. PED = 48 MONTHS. Maternity = 9 MONTHS to 2 YEARS.
• IRDAI Standardized Permanent Exclusions (17): Cosmetic surgery, dental (unless accident), hearing aids, spectacles, congenital external diseases, infertility treatment, self-inflicted injury, war injuries, drug/alcohol abuse. Insurers CANNOT add exclusions beyond IRDAI's 17.
• Loading in Health Insurance: Extra premium for higher-risk individuals (diabetics, hypertension). Alternative = EXCLUDE the specific condition rather than charging extra.
• AYUSH Coverage: IRDAI mandates ALL health policies MUST cover AYUSH treatment (Ayurveda, Yoga, Unani, Siddha, Homeopathy) at IN-PATIENT level, same as allopathy.
• Portability and Underwriting: When switching via portability, new insurer must HONOR the waiting period ALREADY SERVED. Cannot impose fresh waiting period for completed periods.

🎯 HIGHLY REPEATED EXAM Q&A:
Q: Normal BMI range is:
A) 15 to 18  B) 18.5 to 24.9  C) 25 to 29.9  D) 30 and above
A: 18.5 to 24.9

Q: Cosmetic surgery in health insurance is:
A) Covered after 2 years  B) Covered in CI plans  C) A permanent exclusion  D) Covered only in group policies
A: A permanent exclusion

Q: AYUSH treatment coverage in health insurance was mandated by:
A) LIC  B) Ministry of Health  C) IRDAI  D) WHO
A: IRDAI

Q: Maternity benefit waiting period in health insurance is typically:
A) 30 days  B) 3 months  C) 9 months to 2 years  D) 4 years
A: 9 months to 2 years

Q: An applicant with high BMI (obese) may face which outcome?
A) All claims rejected  B) Free policy  C) Premium loading or exclusion  D) Double sum insured
A: Premium loading or exclusion

items.title: Chapter 24: Health Insurance Claims
items.description:
• Types of Health Claims: CASHLESS = treatment at network hospital; insurer pays hospital DIRECTLY. REIMBURSEMENT = treatment at any hospital; insured pays first, claims back from insurer.
• Cashless Process: Admitted to NETWORK HOSPITAL > Hospital sends pre-auth to TPA > TPA approves > Treatment given > Hospital sends final bill > TPA pays hospital directly > Patient pays only non-covered items.
• Reimbursement Process: Treated at ANY hospital > Patient pays all bills > Submits claim form + documents within time limit (30-90 days post discharge) > Insurer verifies and pays.
• IRDAI Claim Timelines: Acknowledge claim within 15 DAYS. Settle or reject within 30 DAYS of receiving ALL documents. If investigation needed > complete within 45 DAYS. Delayed payment = INTEREST payable.
• Co-payment Clause: Insured bears a FIXED PERCENTAGE of each claim (10% or 20%). Common in SENIOR CITIZEN policies. Reduces insurer liability and keeps premium affordable.
• No Claim Bonus (NCB): No claim in a policy year > Sum Insured INCREASES (typically 5-10% per year, MAX 50% cumulative) WITHOUT premium increase. OR PREMIUM DISCOUNT given at renewal. NCB is LOST if a claim is made.
• Common Claim Rejection Reasons: Non-disclosure of PED. Claim during waiting period. Excluded treatment (cosmetic, dental). OPD not covered. Policy lapsed. Fraud or inflated bills.
• TPA Role in Claims: Hospital empanelment, cashless claim processing, pre-auth issuance, claim investigation, coordination between insurer and hospital. TPA does NOT bear financial risk.

🎯 HIGHLY REPEATED EXAM Q&A:
Q: In a cashless health insurance claim, the insurer pays:
A) The insured directly  B) The hospital directly  C) The TPA  D) The government
A: The hospital directly

Q: IRDAI mandates settlement or rejection within how many days of receiving all documents?
A) 15 days  B) 30 days  C) 45 days  D) 60 days
A: 30 days

Q: No Claim Bonus in health insurance means:
A) Free policy next year  B) Double premium refund  C) Increase in Sum Insured or premium discount  D) Special rider free
A: Increase in Sum Insured or premium discount

Q: A co-payment clause in health insurance means:
A) Insurer pays full claim  B) Insured pays a portion of each claim  C) Both insurers share  D) TPA pays first
A: Insured pays a portion of each claim

Q: Reimbursement claims in health insurance should generally be submitted within:
A) 7 days  B) 15 days  C) 30 days  D) 90 days
A: 30 days post discharge
